patch_description: The current program relies entirely on Powell over 33 softmax parameters with three annealing temperatures per start (6 starts → 18 Powell runs), which is slow (24.5s) and gets stuck because softmax-smoothed softmin gradients are weak. A more effective approach for the Heilbronn problem is a fast direct-coordinate "worst-triangle" local search: at each step, identify the minimal-area triangle and push its three vertices away from their opposite sides (the exact gradient of that triangle's area), projecting back via barycentric clipping to maintain feasibility. This exploits the geometry directly (the optimal configuration is characterized by many near-equal minimal triangles) and is very fast. I add this as a cheap pre-optimization stage that produces a high-quality start; Powell then polishes only the single best candidate with a reduced temperature schedule, cutting runtime substantially while improving the final min area. The strictly-positive guard on the returned configuration is preserved.
